errors.accountExists: An account with this email already exists. Sign in instead, or use another email address.
errors.sessionExpired: Your session has ended, for example because this device was signed out elsewhere. Lock and unlock Passbox to continue.
errors.reauthenticate: For your security, confirm this change with your master password again.
errors.notFound: This no longer exists on the server. It may have been deleted on another device.
errors.badRequest: The server did not accept the request. Update Passbox and try again.
errors.server: Something went wrong on the server. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.unexpected: The server answered with an unexpected error ({status}). Try again.
errors.unknown: Something went wrong. Try again, and reload Passbox if it keeps happening.
kit.title: Your Emergency Kit
kit.explain.title: Passbox protects your data with two keys.
kit.explain.body: Your master password (in your head) and your Secret Key (on paper). Like a safe-deposit box at the bank: only both together open the vault. You only need the Secret Key when you set up Passbox on a new device.
kit.explain.noRecovery: Nobody can recover them for you, not even Passbox. Download or print the kit now and keep it somewhere safe.
kit.card.heading: Emergency Kit – keep it safe!
kit.field.passwordLine: Write your master password here if you like
kit.steps.title: New device? Here is how:
kit.steps.2: Choose “Sign in” and enter your email, master password and the Secret Key from this kit.
kit.steps.3: Done. You only need the Secret Key once per device.
kit.storage: Keep the printout with your important documents, or store the PDF somewhere safe outside Passbox. Don't send it by email and don't save it in a spreadsheet.
kit.downloadedHint: It was created on this device; nothing was uploaded. Move it somewhere safe.
kit.check.title: Check your kit
kit.check.label: Enter the last {count} characters of your Secret Key from the PDF or printout
kit.check.wrong: That doesn't match. Compare it with the end of the Secret Key in your kit.
kit.laterHint: Passbox will remind you until the kit is saved.
kit.pdf.title: Passbox Emergency Kit
kit.pdf.intro: Passbox protects your data with two keys: your master password and the Secret Key below. You need both to sign in on a new device. Nobody can recover them for you, not even Passbox.
kit.pdf.passwordHint: Optional: write down your master password by hand. Then keep this page as safe as cash.
kit.pdf.footer: Passbox is in early development and has not been independently audited yet.
kit.reminder.title: Emergency Kit not saved yet
kit.reminder.body: Without the kit you can't get to your data on a new device.
reauth.title: Confirm it's you
reauth.description: Enter your master password to show your Emergency Kit. Passbox checks it on this device.
item.noteLines: Secure note · {count, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
server.error.empty: Enter the address of your Passbox server.
server.error.invalid: This is not a valid address.
server.error.scheme: Use an address that starts with https://.
server.error.credentials: Remove the user name and password from the address.
server.error.query: Remove everything after ? or # from the address.
server.error.insecure: Use https://. Plain http:// is only allowed for a server on this computer (localhost), because anyone on the network could read and change it.
server.error.unreachable: No Passbox server answered at {server}. Check the address and your connection.
server.description: Enter the address of the Passbox server that stores your vault. Your company's IT usually tells you this address.
server.label: Server address
insecure.title: Not secure: this page is loaded over http.
insecure.body: Anyone on the network can change it and read your master password. Ask your administrator for the https:// address.
clipboard.blocked: The browser blocked access to the clipboard.
clipboard.clears: Passbox clears it from the clipboard in {seconds} seconds.
clipboard.clearsWeb: Passbox clears it from the clipboard in {seconds} seconds, or when you return to Passbox if you have switched away.
landing.headline: One password to remember. Passbox takes care of the rest.
landing.point1.title: Only you can see your passwords
landing.point1.text: Not even we can. Everything is locked on your device before it is saved.
landing.point2.title: Strong passwords without the effort
landing.point2.text: Passbox creates them for you and warns you about weak or reused ones.
landing.point3.title: Fills in automatically
landing.point3.text: In your browser and on your phone, on every device you use.
landing.footer: Open source (MIT license) · can run on your own servers
signIn.title: Sign in to Passbox
signIn.description: New on this device? You need your Emergency Kit once.
signUp.title: Create your account
signUp.description: Set up your private vault in about a minute.
welcome.modeLabel: Sign in or create an account
signIn.secretKeyHint: It's in your Emergency Kit. Needed only once per device.
signIn.secretKeyLength: The Secret Key is incomplete: {missing, plural, one {# character is} other {# characters are}} missing.
signUp.passwordHint: The only password you need to remember. Nobody can reset it, not even us. Write it on your Emergency Kit.
signUp.suggestionHint: Easy to remember, hard to guess. Write it down until you know it by heart.
signUp.tooWeak: This password is too easy to guess. Tip: use four or more random words, for example “coffee table cloud bicycle”.
signUp.next: Next, you will save your Emergency Kit with your Secret Key.
signUp.acceptable: Good enough for a master password.
forgot.title: Forgot your master password?
forgot.intro: Passbox can't reset it: nobody knows it but you, not even us. These are the ways back to your data:
forgot.step1: Is Passbox still unlocked on another device, for example your phone? Then set a new master password there under Settings.
forgot.step4: Otherwise only a new account remains. The old data can't be recovered.
errors.emergencyWaiting: The waiting period hasn't ended yet. You'll get access once it does, unless the person declines.
forgot.unlockedBody: While Passbox is unlocked you can set a new master password under Change master password. Now is a good time to prepare for the day you forget it: create a recovery code, allow recovery through your organization or add an emergency contact.
forgot.code.title: With your recovery code
forgot.code.body: It's in your Emergency Kit and starts with R1-. You set a new master password and get a new Secret Key.
forgot.code.missing: This device doesn't know of a recovery code for your account. If you created one on another device, you can still use it.
forgot.org.title: Through your organization or family
forgot.org.body: An administrator verifies that it's really you (by phone or in person) and approves the recovery. This works if you turned it on in Settings.
forgot.org.missing: You haven't allowed recovery through an organization. Ask your administrator; they can't do it without your consent.
forgot.org.pending: You requested recovery on this device. Check whether it was approved.
forgot.device.title: Still unlocked somewhere else?
forgot.emergency.title: Emergency contact
forgot.emergency.body: A trusted person you added can read the vaults you chose after a waiting period. They can't recover your account or change your password.
forgot.newAccount.title: None of these?
recovery.expired: This recovery took too long or was already used. Start again.
recovery.verificationFailed: The recovered key could not be verified, so nothing was changed. Contact your administrator.
recovery.doneHint: Save your new Emergency Kit now: the old Secret Key and recovery code no longer work.
recovery.code.title: Recover with your recovery code
recovery.code.description: Your recovery code is in your Emergency Kit, under your Secret Key. It starts with R1-.
recovery.code.label: Recovery code
recovery.code.hint: Capital or small letters and dashes don't matter. The code is checked on this device first.
recovery.code.invalid: That's not a complete recovery code. Check it against your Emergency Kit: 11 groups of 5 characters after R1-.
recovery.code.wrong: The email or recovery code is wrong. Check both against your Emergency Kit.
recovery.code.needsSecurityKey: Your account's only second factor is a security key, which this recovery doesn't support yet. Ask your organization or the server's administrators.
recovery.code.whatHappens: Next you set a new master password. Passbox then creates a new Secret Key and a new recovery code, and signs out all your other devices.
recovery.twoFactor.title: Confirm with your second factor
recovery.twoFactor.description: Your account uses two-factor sign-in, so the recovery code alone isn't enough.
recovery.twoFactor.label: 6-digit code or two-factor recovery code
recovery.twoFactor.hint: Use the code from your authenticator app, or one of the ten two-factor recovery codes (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) you saved when you set it up.
recovery.newPassword.verified: Verified. You can now set a new master password.
recovery.newPassword.title: Choose a new master password
recovery.newPassword.description: Use one you haven't used before. Passbox can't show it to you later.
recovery.newPassword.newSecretKey: You get a new Secret Key and a new recovery code. The old ones stop working.
recovery.newPassword.signOut: All your other devices are signed out. Sign in there with the new Emergency Kit.
recovery.org.title: Request recovery through your organization
recovery.org.description: Your administrators can let you set a new master password, if you allowed this in Settings.
recovery.org.step1: You send a request from this device.
recovery.org.step2: An administrator calls you or talks to you in person, and you read them the code shown on this device.
recovery.org.step3: Once they approve, you set a new master password here.
recovery.org.privacy: Your administrators never see your passwords. To protect accounts, the answer looks the same whether or not this email can be recovered.
recovery.org.waitingBody: Your administrators got an email. Keep this page open or come back later on this device.
recovery.org.codeLabel: Read this code to your administrator
recovery.org.codeHint: They must see exactly the same code in Passbox. If it differs, they must not approve.
recovery.org.pendingNotice: Your recovery request is waiting for approval.
recovery.org.status.denied.title: Request declined
recovery.org.status.denied.body: An administrator declined the request. Contact your organization if you have questions.
recovery.org.status.expired.title: Request expired
recovery.org.status.expired.body: Requests are valid for two days. Send a new one.
recovery.org.status.cancelled.title: Request withdrawn
recovery.org.status.cancelled.body: This request is no longer active. A newer request replaces older ones.
recovery.org.status.completed.title: Already recovered
recovery.org.status.completed.body: This request was already used to set a new master password.
recovery.org.unverified: The organization's recovery key could not be verified. Ask your administrator to set it up again.
recovery.org.notSetUp: Your organization hasn't set up account recovery yet.
recovery.org.notSetUpAdmin: Not set up yet. Members can only allow it once you set it up.
recovery.org.available: Off. Turn it on so your administrators can help if you forget your master password.
recovery.org.enrolled: On. {count, plural, one {# administrator} other {# administrators}} can approve a recovery after checking it's you.
recovery.org.setUpBody: Passbox creates a recovery key on this device and keeps it for you. Members who agree can then be recovered by you after you checked their identity. Your device briefly holds their account key while approving, so only approve requests you verified in person or by phone.
recovery.org.enrollBody: If you forget your master password, an administrator of {name} can let you set a new one after verifying it's you. Every recovery is logged and you get an email.
recovery.org.enrollHonest: To be honest: an administrator who approves a recovery could technically read your data. Only allow this if you trust them.
recovery.org.enrollDone: Recovery through your organization is on
recovery.org.withdrawBody: Your administrators can no longer recover your account. Make sure you have your recovery code or your master password.
recovery.org.withdrawDone: Recovery through your organization is off
recovery.org.guest: Guests are never recovered by an organization: your account stays only yours.
recovery.org.requiredHint: Your organization requires this. Its admins can restore your access if you forget your master password.
recovery.org.turnOffRequired: Your policy requires recovery. Turn off “Require recovery” in Policies first.
recovery.org.turnOffBody: The recovery key and every member's recovery share are deleted, and open requests are cancelled. Members who forget their master password can then only use their own recovery code. You can set recovery up again later; members then have to allow it again.
recovery.org.turnOffDone: Recovery through the organization is off
recovery.org.addAdminBody: They receive a copy of the recovery key, sealed for their verified key.
recovery.org.enrolledMembers: {count, plural, =0 {No member has turned it on yet.} one {# member turned it on.} other {# members turned it on.}}
recovery.panel.title: Recovery
recovery.panel.description: How you get back to your data if you forget your master password.
recovery.requests.title: Recovery requests
recovery.requests.description: Members who forgot their master password and asked for help. Approve a request only after you verified the person.
recovery.requests.noOrgsHint: Recovery requests appear here for owners and admins.
recovery.requests.open: {count, plural, =0 {View requests} one {# open request} other {# open requests}}
recovery.requests.denyBody: {email} gets an email that the request was declined.
recovery.requests.step1Body: Call them on a number you already know, or talk in person. Don't use contact details from the request or an email: an attacker could have sent it.
recovery.requests.identityConfirmed: I spoke with {email} myself and I'm sure the request is theirs.
recovery.requests.step2Body: Ask them to read the code shown on their screen. Approve only if it is exactly this code.
recovery.requests.codeConfirmed: The code on their screen is exactly the same.
recovery.requests.honest: While approving, your device briefly holds this member's account key and passes it on, sealed for their device. Passbox logs the recovery and notifies the member and all recovery admins.
recovery.requests.approvedHint: They can now set a new master password on their device.
recoveryCode.title: Account recovery code
recoveryCode.active: Created on {date}. It's in your Emergency Kit and lets you set a new master password if you forget it.
recoveryCode.inactive: Not set up. With a recovery code you can set a new master password if you forget it.
recoveryCode.replaceBody: The current code stops working. Print or download the new Emergency Kit afterwards.
recoveryCode.removeBody: Without it you can only recover your account through your organization, if you allowed that. Your master password and Secret Key keep working.
recoveryCode.checkLabel: Type the last {count} characters of the recovery code from your PDF or printout
recoveryCode.checkWrong: That doesn't match. Compare it with the end of the recovery code in your kit.
recoveryCode.signUpLabel: Add a recovery code to my Emergency Kit
recoveryCode.signUpDescription: Recommended. If you forget your master password, the code lets you set a new one. Keep the kit as safe as cash.
recoveryCode.signUpFailed: The recovery code could not be created
kit.recoveredHint: You have a new Secret Key and a new recovery code. The old kit no longer works: destroy it and keep this one.
kit.explain.withRecoveryCode: If you forget your master password, the recovery code in this kit lets you set a new one. Anyone who has this kit and knows your email can do that too, so keep it as safe as cash.
kit.recoveryCodeHint: Only if you forget your master password: Sign in → Forgot your master password? → Enter recovery code.
kit.pdf.introRecovery: Passbox protects your data with two keys: your master password and the Secret Key below. If you forget the master password, the recovery code below lets you set a new one. Nobody else can recover them, not even Passbox.
kit.pdf.recoveryCodeHint: Only if you forget your master password. Anyone with this page and your email can recover your account.
emergency.title: Emergency access
emergency.description: A trusted person can read the vaults you choose if something happens to you, after a waiting period in which you can decline.
emergency.myContactsHint: They need a Passbox account. You can remove them at any time.
emergency.addDescription: We'll email them an invitation. After they accept, you choose which vaults they may read.
emergency.emailHint: The email of their Passbox account (or the one they'll sign up with).
emergency.waitHint: When they ask for access, you get an email and can decline during this time.
emergency.scopeBody: Read access to the personal vaults you choose. They can't change anything, see shared vaults or recover your account.
emergency.addedHint: Once they accept, confirm them here and choose the vaults.
emergency.grantedMeta: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} waiting period · {vaults, plural, =0 {no vaults yet} one {# vault} other {# vaults}}
emergency.invitedHint: Waiting for them to accept the invitation.
emergency.confirmDescription: Choose what they may read after a waiting period of {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
emergency.vaultsHint: Only personal vaults. Vaults you create later are not included unless you add them.
emergency.fingerprintHint: To be completely sure, compare it with them (Settings → Technical details on their device). The vault keys are sealed for this key only.
emergency.keyChanged: Their key changed since you last saw it. Compare the fingerprint with them before you continue.
emergency.requestedGrantor: Access requested. They get read access on {date} ({days, plural, one {in # day} other {in # days}}) unless you decline.
emergency.approveBody: {email} can read the shared vaults right away, without waiting.
emergency.denyBody: They don't get access and receive an email. They can ask again later.
emergency.endBody: They can't open the vaults anymore. What they already saw, they may have kept: change important passwords.
emergency.trustMeHint: You can ask for access to their vaults in an emergency.
emergency.receivedMeta: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} waiting period
emergency.declineBody: {email} will no longer have you as emergency contact.
emergency.requestBody: {email} gets an email right away and can decline. If they don't, you can read their shared vaults after {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
emergency.countdown: Access in {days, plural, =0 {less than a day} one {# day} other {# days}} (from {date}), unless they decline.
emergency.wasDenied: Your last request was declined on {date}.
emergency.footnote: The vaults stay encrypted for your contact's key. The waiting period is enforced by the server.
emergency.view.title: Emergency access: {email}
emergency.view.description: The vaults this person shared with you for emergencies.
emergency.view.readOnly: Read only. The data is decrypted on this device and not stored.
emergency.view.errors: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} could not be decrypted.
addDevice.title: Add a device
addDevice.description: Sign in on a new device without typing the Secret Key: show a code here and enter it there.
addDevice.dialogDescription: Enter this code on the new device.
addDevice.qrLabel: QR code with the device code
addDevice.step1: Open Passbox on the new device.
addDevice.step2: On the sign-in screen, choose “Use a code from another device” and enter the code.
addDevice.step3: Confirm the new device here, then enter your master password there.
addDevice.privacy: Your master password is never sent.
addDevice.claimedBody: Was that you? If you approve, it receives your email and Secret Key, encrypted for that device. It still needs your master password.
addDevice.done: Done. Enter your master password on the new device.
addDevice.expired: The code expired. Show a new one.
addDevice.mismatch: Something isn't right: the device didn't prove it knows the code. Nothing was sent. Show a new code.
linkDevice.link: Use a code from another device
linkDevice.title: Sign in with another device
linkDevice.description: Use a device where Passbox is already open. You don't need to type the Secret Key.
linkDevice.step1: On the other device, open Settings → Recovery → Add a device.
linkDevice.step3: Confirm on the other device, then enter your master password here.
linkDevice.format: The code has 16 characters, like ABCD-EFGH-JKMN-PQRS.
linkDevice.invalid: This code doesn't work (anymore). Show a new code on your other device.
linkDevice.privacy: Your master password is never sent. The other device sends your email and Secret Key, encrypted for this device.
linkDevice.waitingBody: Your other device now asks whether to add this one.

change.title: Change the password for {name}
change.description: Three short steps. Passbox keeps your current password until you confirm that the change worked.
change.step1.title: Open the website and sign in
change.step1.text: Open {site} and sign in with your current password. Then go to the page where you can change your password (often under Settings › Security).
change.step2.title: Paste the new password on the website
change.step2.text: Passbox created a new, strong password. Copy it and paste it into the website's “new password” field.
change.step3.title: Did it work?
change.step3.text: Only save if the website accepted the new password. Your current password is kept under “Previous passwords”.
change.savedHint: The previous one is under “Previous passwords”.
change.saveFailed: The new password could not be saved
change.kept: Nothing changed. Your current password is still saved.
trash.movedHint: You can restore it for 30 days.
trash.moveFailed: Could not move the item to the trash
detail.none.title: No item selected
detail.none.text: Choose an item from the list, or press {shortcut} to search everything.
detail.warning.weak: This password is easy to guess. Change it on the website and let Passbox create a strong one.
detail.warning.reused: You also use this password for {count, plural, one {# other account} other {# other accounts}}. If one is hacked, all of them are at risk.
detail.warning.insecure: This website address starts with http://, so the connection is not encrypted.
detail.totpInvalid: Can't create a code – check the setup key
history.confirmText: It becomes the current password again. The current one moves to “Previous passwords”, so nothing is lost.
history.restoredHint: Make sure the website still accepts it.
editor.title: Title
editor.notesPlaceholder: Anything else worth remembering. Notes are encrypted too.
editor.tagsPlaceholder: Type a tag and press Enter
editor.discardText: Your unsaved changes will be lost.
editor.duplicate.title: You already have a login for {site}
editor.duplicate.text: “{name}” uses the same username ({username}). Update it with what you entered, or keep both?
totp.hint: Optional. Passbox then creates the 6-digit codes for you, like Google or Microsoft Authenticator.
totp.guide.1: On the website (for example Salesforce), open Settings › Security › Two-factor or Authenticator app.
totp.guide.2: Take a screenshot of the QR code and choose “QR code from image” or “Paste QR code”. Or choose “Enter key manually” on the website and paste the text here.
totp.guide.3: Save, then enter the 6-digit code Passbox shows on the website.
qr.error.noImage: There is no image on the clipboard. Copy a screenshot of the QR code first.
qr.error.clipboard: The browser didn't allow reading the clipboard. Choose “QR code from image” instead, or paste the image into the field.
qr.error.noCode: No QR code found in this image. Use a sharp screenshot that shows the whole code.
qr.error.notTotp: This QR code doesn't contain a two-factor setup key.
qr.error.migration: This is an export code from Google Authenticator. Scan the QR code on the website instead.
qr.error.unreadable: This image could not be read.

start.title: Getting started
start.description: A few steps so Passbox works everywhere and you never get locked out.
start.account.title: Account created
start.kit.title: Save your Emergency Kit
start.kit.text: Without it you can't sign in on a new device.
start.extension.title: Install the browser extension
start.extension.text: Passbox fills in your passwords automatically and offers to save new ones.
start.import.title: Import your passwords
start.import.text: Bring them over from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, a spreadsheet (CSV) or another password manager.
start.import.manual: Save the first login by hand
start.phone.title: Set up your phone
start.phone.text: Install Passbox on your phone and sign in once with your Emergency Kit.
start.security.title: Look at the security check
start.security.text: See which passwords are easy to guess or used more than once.
security.description: The check runs on this device. Passwords never leave it; only optional checks send a short hash prefix or an email address you confirmed.
security.none.title: Nothing to check yet
security.none.text: Save logins, cards and documents, and the security check shows what to improve, most important first.
security.breach.title: Check for leaked passwords
security.breach.consent: Passbox asks the free service Have I Been Pwned whether your passwords appear in known data breaches. Your passwords never leave this device: only the first 5 characters of a hash of each password are sent, and the answer is compared here (k-anonymity).
security.breach.failed: Have I Been Pwned could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
generator.description: Created on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere.
generator.modeHint.password: Random letters, digits and symbols. The strongest choice for websites where Passbox fills in for you.
generator.modeHint.words: Random words. Easy to type on a phone or TV, and easy to remember.
generator.modeHint.readable: No characters that look alike (l, 1, I, O, 0) and no symbols, so you can read it out on the phone.
generator.modeHint.pin: Digits only, for example for a device or a door.
generator.ambiguousHint: Leave out l, 1, I, O and 0, which are easy to confuse
settings.description: Your account, your devices and the preferences on this device.
settings.kitDescription: Download or print it again, for example for a new device. Passbox asks for your master password first.
settings.secretKeyDescription: Stored on this device. To sign in elsewhere, use your Emergency Kit.
settings.passwordDescription: Change it while you know it. Nobody can reset it for you.
settings.contentsValue: {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} in {vaults, plural, one {# vault} other {# vaults}}
settings.autoLockDescription: Lock the vault after this time without activity.
settings.afterMinutes: After {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
settings.clipboardDescription: Remove copied passwords from the clipboard.
settings.lockOnClose: Lock when the window is closed
settings.lockOnCloseDescription: Passbox keeps running in the tray after you close the window.
settings.lockNowDescription: Removes all keys and decrypted data from memory.
settings.serverDescription: To use a different server, sign out of this device.
settings.encryptionValue: XChaCha20-Poly1305 · keys from Argon2id and HKDF · sign-in with OPAQUE
settings.signOutDescription: Removes your account and Secret Key from this device. Your data stays safe on the server.
devices.description: Where your account is signed in. Sign out a device you no longer use or have lost.
devices.confirmText: The device has to sign in again with the master password. It keeps the Secret Key if it already has it, so change your master password too if the device was lost.
devices.othersText: {count, plural, one {# device has} other {# devices have}} to sign in again. This device stays signed in.
devices.revokeFailed: Could not sign out the device
activity.description: The last 50 security events of your account.
activity.footnote: Sign-in attempts with a wrong master password are detected on the device and may not appear here.
changeMaster.title: Change master password

sharing.title: Family & team
sharing.description: Share passwords with the people you trust. Shared vaults are end-to-end encrypted: the server stores them but cannot read them.
sharing.overview.summary: {people, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} · {vaults, plural, one {# shared vault} other {# shared vaults}}
sharing.overview.pendingSummary: You'll see the shared vaults once you are confirmed.
sharing.overview.waiting: {count, plural, one {# waiting for you} other {# waiting for you}}
sharing.startFamily.title: Start a family
sharing.startFamily.text: Share Wi-Fi, streaming and bank logins at home. A family vault is created for you, and you are the organizer.
sharing.startTeam.title: Create a team
sharing.startTeam.text: For colleagues: shared vaults per project or department, groups, and roles for who may change what.
sharing.join.title: Got an invitation?
sharing.join.text: Opening the link from the email is enough. If you are in the desktop app, paste the link here.
sharing.join.label: Invitation link
sharing.join.invalid: This doesn't look like a Passbox invitation link. Copy the whole link from the email, including everything after #.
sharing.howSafe.title: How Passbox protects what you share
sharing.howSafe.p1: Every shared vault has its own key. Passbox locks it separately for each member on their device, so the server only ever stores encrypted data.
sharing.howSafe.p2: Before someone gets access, an organizer or admin confirms them. Passbox checks their key and shows a security code you can compare in person or on the phone.
sharing.howSafe.p3: When someone leaves, Passbox replaces the vault keys so they can't read anything new. What they saw before, they may have kept – so change important passwords.
sharing.create.familyText: Give your family a name. Only members can see it.
sharing.create.familyPoint1: A family vault is created that everyone in the family can use.
sharing.create.familyPoint2: You are the organizer: you invite people and decide who sees what.
sharing.create.familyDone: “{name}” is ready. Invite your family next.
sharing.create.teamText: Name the team, for example after your company or department. Only members can see it.
sharing.create.teamDone: Team “{name}” created. Invite colleagues and create shared vaults next.
sharing.create.nameHint: Encrypted: the server never sees the name.
sharing.create.recoveryFamily: Account recovery is on: if someone in the family forgets their master password, you as the organizer can restore their access after checking it's them. Everyone sees this when they join; you can turn it off in the family's settings.
sharing.create.recoveryTeam: Account recovery is on: if a member forgets their master password, an admin can restore their access after checking it's them. Members see this when they join; you can turn it off under Administration → Recovery.
sharing.org.gone: This family or team no longer exists, or you are no longer a member.
sharing.org.suspended: Your membership is paused. You can't open the shared vaults until an organizer or admin lifts the pause.
sharing.org.unverified: Passbox could not verify this organization's signature. Shared vaults stay locked. Ask the organizer to check, or open the invitation link again.
sharing.role.family.owner.description: Created the family and manages everything.
sharing.role.family.admin.description: Can invite and confirm family members and create shared vaults.
sharing.role.family.member.description: Uses the vaults shared with them, for example the family vault.
sharing.role.family.guest.description: Free and view-only: opens, copies and fills only the vaults shared with them, and does not see the other family members.
sharing.role.team.owner.description: Created the team and manages everything, including admins.
sharing.role.team.admin.description: Can invite and confirm members, create vaults and groups.
sharing.role.team.member.description: Uses the vaults shared with them or their groups.
sharing.role.team.guest.description: For external people, free: opens, copies and fills only the vaults shared with them; cannot create or change anything and does not see the member list.
sharing.role.title: Role of {name}
sharing.members.title: Members
sharing.members.limited: You see yourself and the organizers. Everyone else becomes visible once you are a confirmed member.
sharing.members.accepted: Accepted the invitation and waits for confirmation.
sharing.members.acceptedAdmin: Accepted the invitation. Confirm to give access.
sharing.members.codeText: If you want to be sure, compare it with {name} in person or on the phone. {name} finds it under Family & team or in Settings.
sharing.invite.title: Invite to {name}
sharing.invite.familyText: Enter the email address the person uses (or will use) for Passbox.
sharing.invite.teamText: Enter your colleague's work email address. They sign in or create an account with it.
sharing.invite.mailSent: We emailed an invitation to {email}. You can also pass on the link yourself.
sharing.invite.mailOff: This server doesn't send email yet. Send {email} this link yourself, for example by message.
sharing.invite.mailMaybe: If this server sends email, an invitation to {email} is on its way. Faster and safer: pass on the link yourself.
sharing.invite.linkHint: Valid until {date}, only for {email}. The part after # contains a check code for your organization, so nobody can redirect the invitation. Send the whole link.
sharing.invite.next1: {email} opens the link and signs in or creates an account.
sharing.invite.next2: {email} accepts. You'll then see a “Confirm” button here.
sharing.invite.next3Family: You confirm {email} – and the family vault appears for them.
sharing.invite.next3Team: You confirm {email} and share vaults with them or their group.
sharing.invitations.title: Open invitations
sharing.invitations.description: Not accepted yet. Invitations expire after 7 days.
sharing.invitations.revokeText: The link stops working right away. You can invite the person again at any time.
sharing.confirm.title: Confirm {name}
sharing.confirm.text: Before {name} gets access, Passbox checks their key in the key directory. Only confirm people you invited.
sharing.confirm.compareText: Compare these numbers on the phone or in person. {name} sees their code right after accepting the invitation. If both match, nobody in between – not even the server – swapped the key.
sharing.confirm.changed: The security code of {name} changed since this device last saw it. Only continue after comparing the code with {name}.
sharing.confirm.familyVault: {name} will then see the family vault and can add and change entries in it.
sharing.confirm.done: {name} is confirmed. Share vaults with them now.
sharing.confirm.doneFamily: {name} is confirmed and now sees the family vault.
sharing.suspend.title: Pause access for {name}?
sharing.suspend.text: The server stops giving {name} the shared vaults until you lift the pause. This is a server-side block: to remove access for good and replace the keys, remove {name} instead.
sharing.suspend.reactivateText: {name} can use the shared vaults again.
sharing.remove.title: Remove {name}?
sharing.remove.text: {name} will no longer be a member.
sharing.remove.consequence: {name} loses access immediately. Anything {name} has already seen, they may have kept – change important passwords.
sharing.remove.rotation: Passbox replaces the keys of these vaults and re-encrypts their entries. This can take a moment.
sharing.remove.doneText: The vaults have new keys. {name} can't read anything new.
sharing.remove.changePasswords: Change the important passwords {name} could see, such as online banking, email and streaming.
sharing.vaults.title: Shared vaults
sharing.vaults.description: Everything in a shared vault is visible to its members.
sharing.vaults.newText: A vault for {name}. Next you choose who can see it.
sharing.vaultRole.view.description: Can see, copy and fill entries, but not change them.
sharing.vaultRole.edit.description: Can add, change and delete entries.
sharing.vaultRole.manage.description: Can also decide who has access.
sharing.viewNote.text: “View” is enforced by the server: it refuses changes. To show entries, a person's device needs the vault key, and with that key a modified app could technically create new entries. Share only with people you trust; for strict separation, use a separate vault.
sharing.vaultDialog.title: Who has access to “{vault}”
sharing.vaultDialog.text: Shared in {org}. Everyone listed can see all entries in this vault.
sharing.vaultDialog.nobodyLeft: Everyone in the organization already has access. Invite more people first.
sharing.vaultDialog.waiting: {count, plural, one {# person still waits} other {# people still wait}} for confirmation and can be added afterwards.
sharing.vaultDialog.onlyManagers: Only people with “Manage” can change who has access.
sharing.vaultDialog.removeText: {name} loses access to this vault immediately. Passbox replaces the vault key so {name} can't read anything new. What {name} has already seen, they may have kept – change important passwords.
sharing.rotation.pendingManager: Someone left this vault. Replace the key so they can't read new entries.
sharing.rotation.pendingMember: Someone left this vault. A manager's device will replace the key soon.
sharing.rotation.running: Securing {count, plural, one {a shared vault} other {# shared vaults}}…
sharing.rotation.runningHint: Someone left. Passbox replaces the keys so they can't read anything new.
sharing.rotation.finished: {count, plural, one {Shared vault secured} other {# shared vaults secured}}.
sharing.group.title: Groups
sharing.group.description: Share a vault with a group once instead of with every person. New group members get access to all of the group's vaults.
sharing.group.newText: For example a department or project. You can share vaults with the group afterwards.
sharing.group.name: Group name
sharing.group.youAreMember: You are always a member of the groups you create.
sharing.group.deleteText: Members keep their own access to vaults, but lose what they had through this group. Remove the group from its vaults first.
sharing.group.membersText: Adding a person gives them access to every vault of the group.
sharing.group.notMember: Only admins who are members of this group can change its members.
sharing.group.removeHint: Removing a person replaces the group key and the keys of the group's vaults.
sharing.settings.title: Settings
sharing.settings.renameText: The name is encrypted; only members see it.
sharing.settings.name: Name
sharing.settings.leaveText: You lose access to all shared vaults of this organization.
sharing.settings.leaveConfirm: You lose access to all shared vaults of {name} immediately. To join again, you need a new invitation.
sharing.settings.deleteText: Deletes all shared vaults and their entries for everyone. This can't be undone.
sharing.settings.deleteConfirm: All shared vaults of {name} and every entry in them are deleted permanently, for all members. Move entries you want to keep to your private vault first.
sharing.accept.titleFamilyAnon: You are invited to a family
sharing.accept.titleTeamAnon: You are invited to a team
sharing.accept.step2: {name} confirms you. If you like, compare your security codes on the phone.
sharing.accept.step3Family: Then you see the family vault in Passbox.
sharing.accept.step3Team: Then you see the vaults shared with you.
sharing.accept.privacy: Your private vault stays private. Only what is in shared vaults is shared.
sharing.accept.guest: As a guest you can open, copy and fill the entries of vaults shared with you. You cannot create or change anything. Guests are free.
sharing.accept.recoveryTitleFamily: The organizer can restore your access
sharing.accept.recoveryTitleTeam: The team's admins can restore your access
sharing.accept.recoveryBody: When you join, Passbox seals a recovery share of your account for them. If you forget your master password, they can let you set a new one after checking it's you. To do that, the approving admin's device briefly holds your account key and could technically read your data. Every recovery is logged and you get an email. Accept only if you trust them.
sharing.accept.wrongAccount: This invitation is for {invited}, but you are signed in as {current}. Sign out and sign in (or create an account) with {invited}, then open the link again.
sharing.accept.done: Invitation accepted. You'll get access once you're confirmed.
sharing.accept.invalid: This invitation is no longer valid: it expired, was withdrawn or was already used. Ask for a new one.
sharing.accept.signInFirst: Sign in or create an account with {email} first. Then you can accept the invitation.
sharing.waiting.title: Waiting for confirmation
sharing.waiting.text: You accepted the invitation. {name} still has to confirm you. Passbox checks automatically – you'll see the shared vaults right afterwards.
sharing.waiting.compare: If {name} asks, read out these numbers. They prove that it's really your account.
sharing.securityCode.title: Your security code
sharing.securityCode.description: These numbers identify your keys. People who share with you can compare them to make sure nobody in between swapped your key.
sharing.securityCode.when: You only need it when someone asks, for example when confirming you in a family or team. It isn't secret, but it never changes unless your keys do.
sharing.securityCode.missing: Your keys are being set up. Sync once and check again.
sharing.securityCode.ok: The server lists exactly this code for your account.
sharing.securityCode.mismatch: The server lists a different key for your account. Don't share anything new and contact your administrator.
sharing.viewOnly.title: View only.
sharing.viewOnly.text: You can see, copy and fill this entry, but not change it. Whoever manages the vault can give you edit rights.
sharing.viewOnly.list: View only: you can use these entries but not change them.
sharing.guest.title: You are a guest.
sharing.guest.text: You can see, copy and fill this entry, but not change it, share it or create anything here. Ask an admin of the organization to make you a member if you need more.
sharing.guest.list: Guest: you can use these entries but not change, share or add any.
sharing.shareItem.title: Share “{name}”
sharing.shareItem.text: Passbox shares whole vaults. To share this entry, move it into a shared vault.
sharing.shareItem.howItWorks: Earlier passwords of this entry are not shared. The original goes to the trash and can be restored for 30 days.
sharing.shareItem.doneHint: The original is in the trash for 30 days.
sharing.shareItem.noOrg: To share, start a family or a team first. It takes a minute.
sharing.shareItem.noVault: You have no shared vault you may add entries to yet.
sharing.keyChange.how: Call {name} or meet in person and compare the numbers. Only accept if they match.
sharing.keyChange.accept: Code matches – trust the new key
sharing.keyChange.accepted: Passbox trusts the new key of {name}.
sharing.warning.banner.keyChanged: A member's security code changed. Compare it before sharing anything new.
sharing.warning.banner.ownKey: Passbox sees a different key for your own account. Check it in Settings.
sharing.warning.banner.integrity: Passbox couldn't verify some shared data and keeps it locked.
sharing.warning.banner.mismatch: The server reports different permissions than Passbox verified.
sharing.warning.title: Sharing needs your attention
sharing.warning.intro: Passbox checks every member, key and permission itself instead of trusting the server. Here is what didn't add up.
sharing.warning.keyChanged.title: New security code for {name}
sharing.warning.keyChanged.text: This usually means {name} set up their account again. Rarely, it can be an attack. Until you compare it, Passbox shares nothing new with {name}.
sharing.warning.ownKey.title: Your own key looks different
sharing.warning.ownKey.text: The organization lists a key for your account that isn't the one on this device. Don't share anything new and tell the organizer or admin.
sharing.warning.integrity.title: Couldn't verify: {name}
sharing.warning.integrity.text: A signature or member list didn't check out, so Passbox keeps it locked rather than trusting it. This can be a temporary error or a problem on the server. Ask the organizer or admin to share it again.
sharing.warning.mismatch.title: Different permissions: {name}
sharing.warning.mismatch.text: The server reports permissions that differ from the signed ones. Passbox shows and uses the signed ones. Usually this resolves itself after the next change.
sharing.error.alreadyMember: This person is already a member.
sharing.error.conflict: Something changed in the meantime. Passbox loaded the latest state – try again.
sharing.error.guestViewOnly: Guests can only open, copy and fill entries. Ask an admin of the organization to make you a member.
sharing.error.rotated: The vault got a new key in the meantime. Passbox loaded it – try again.
sharing.error.forbidden: You don't have permission for this. Ask the organizer or an admin.
sharing.error.notFound: This no longer exists. It may have been withdrawn, used or deleted.
sharing.error.keyChanged: This person's security code changed. Compare it first (Details in the yellow banner), then try again.
sharing.error.unverified: Passbox couldn't verify this person's key yet. Try again after a sync.
security.score.label: Security score {score} of 100: {rating}
security.score.explain: Every login counts the same. Each one loses points for its open problems; a breached password costs all of them. Dismissed findings don't count. {count, plural, one {Fixing # item} other {Fixing the # items}} below brings the most.
security.summaryCategories: {count, plural, one {# kind of problem} other {# kinds of problems}} across {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}. Start at the top; most fixes take two minutes.
security.fixFirst.title: Fix these first
security.fixFirst.text: The items that raise your score the most.
security.categories.title: All checks
security.categories.allDismissed: All findings of this kind are dismissed.
security.dismiss.label: Dismiss for {item}
security.dismissed.title: Dismissed ({count})
security.dismissed.toast: Finding dismissed. It no longer counts for the score.
security.detail.similarPrevious: Only slightly changed from its previous password
security.detail.age: Set {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
security.detail.expiring: Expires {date} (in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}})
security.breach.routeServer: The request goes through your Passbox server, so Have I Been Pwned doesn't see your IP address.
security.breach.routeDirect: The request goes directly to Have I Been Pwned, which can see your IP address.
security.breach.failedServer: Your Passbox server couldn't check the passwords. Try again later, or allow a direct check in the settings below.
security.settings.title: Settings for the security check
security.settings.routeHint.auto: Through your Passbox server when it offers it, otherwise directly.
security.settings.routeHint.server: Only through your Passbox server; Have I Been Pwned never sees your IP address.
security.settings.routeHint.direct: Directly from this device; Have I Been Pwned sees your IP address.
security.settings.noProxy: Your server doesn't offer this right now.
security.monitor.title: Email breach monitoring
security.monitor.text: Your Passbox server checks your email addresses with Have I Been Pwned regularly and emails you when one shows up in a new data breach.
security.monitor.unavailable: Not set up on this server. Its administrators can turn it on with a Have I Been Pwned API key (PASSBOX_HIBP_API_KEY).
security.monitor.consent: This sends the email address (never a password) from your Passbox server to Have I Been Pwned. The server stores the address and the results until you remove it. You confirm each address with a code sent to it.
security.monitor.codeSent: Code sent. Enter it below to start monitoring.
security.monitor.removeText: The server deletes {email} and its results. You can add it again later.
security.kind.breached.title: Found in data breaches
security.kind.breached.text: These passwords appear in known data breaches. Attackers try them first, on every site.
security.kind.breached.fix: Change the password on the website now and let Passbox create a new one. If you used it elsewhere, change it there too.
security.kind.exposed_email.title: Account in a data breach
security.kind.exposed_email.summary: Your email address was in a breach of this site.
security.kind.exposed_email.text: Email monitoring found the address of this login in a data breach of the same website. The password may have been exposed too.
security.kind.exposed_email.fix: Change the password on this website and turn on two-factor sign-in if it offers it.
security.kind.breached_site.title: Breached website
security.kind.breached_site.summary: The website had a data breach after you set the password.
security.kind.breached_site.text: Have I Been Pwned lists a data breach of this website that became public after the password was set. Passbox compares the public list with your logins on this device; nobody learns which websites you use.
security.kind.breached_site.fix: Change the password on the website now – Passbox suggests a strong new one – and turn on two-factor sign-in if the site offers it. If you used the same password elsewhere, change it there too.
security.breachedSite.affected: {site} had a data breach on {date} ({data}). Your password is older. Change it now.
security.breachedSite.possibly: {site} had a data breach on {date} ({data}). It is not known when you set this password – change it to be safe.
security.breachedSite.affectedUndated: {site} had a data breach ({data}). Your password is older. Change it now.
security.breachedSite.possiblyUndated: {site} had a data breach ({data}). It is not known when you set this password – change it to be safe.
security.breachedSite.factsText: Facts from Have I Been Pwned's public list of breached websites. Passbox compares it with your logins on this device.
security.breachAlert.titleMany: {count, plural, one {# new data breach} other {# new data breaches}} of your websites
security.breachAlert.body: {count, plural, one {# of your logins is affected.} other {# of your logins are affected.}} Change the passwords in the security check.
security.breachAlert.notifyOn: You get a notification when a website of your logins has a new data breach.
security.breachAlert.notifyBlocked: Notifications are blocked in this browser. New breaches show as a notice at the top instead.
security.breachAlert.notifyAsk: Get a notification when a website of your logins has a new data breach. The check runs on this device.
security.kind.lookalike.title: Lookalike website address
security.kind.lookalike.text: The saved address looks like another domain: swapped letters, look-alike characters or letters from another alphabet. Phishing sites use this trick.
security.kind.lookalike.fix: Check that the address is the real website. If you entered your password on a fake site, change it on the real one.
security.kind.reused.title: Used more than once
security.kind.reused.summary: The same password on several sites.
security.kind.reused.text: If one of these sites is hacked, attackers can sign in to the others with the same password.
security.kind.reused.fix: Give each login its own password. Start with email and work accounts.
security.kind.weak.title: Easy to guess
security.kind.weak.text: These passwords can be guessed in seconds to hours with common attack lists.
security.kind.weak.fix: Change it on the website and let Passbox create a strong one.
security.kind.similar.title: Similar passwords
security.kind.similar.text: These passwords differ only by a number or symbol (Summer2023!, Summer2024!). Attackers who know one try the variations first.
security.kind.similar.fix: Replace them with passwords Passbox creates; you don't have to remember them.
security.kind.insecure_url.title: Unsecured connection (http)
security.kind.insecure_url.text: These addresses start with http://, so what you send can be read and changed on the way.
security.kind.insecure_url.fix: Check whether the site works with https:// and change the saved address.
security.kind.missing_two_factor.title: Two-factor sign-in available
security.kind.missing_two_factor.summary: Sites that offer 2FA you don't use here.
security.kind.missing_two_factor.text: According to 2fa.directory these sites offer two-factor sign-in, but this login has no one-time code or passkey. A stolen password alone would be enough to sign in.
security.kind.missing_two_factor.fix: Turn on two-factor sign-in on the website and save the setup key in Passbox. Already using an app or security key? Dismiss the finding.
security.kind.expired.title: Expired
security.kind.expired.summary: Cards and documents past their date.
security.kind.expired.text: These cards or documents have expired. Payments and autofill with them will fail.
security.kind.expired.fix: Enter the new card or document, or move the item to the trash.
security.kind.expiring.title: Expires soon
security.kind.expiring.text: These cards or documents expire soon.
security.kind.expiring.fix: Renew them in time and update the expiry date.
security.kind.old.title: Not changed for a long time
security.kind.old.text: Strong, unique passwords don't need regular changes. Old ones are worth a look if they might have been exposed over the years.
security.kind.old.fix: Change it if the account is important or you have used the password elsewhere.
security.kind.passkey_available.title: Passkey available
security.kind.passkey_available.summary: Sites where you could sign in with a passkey.
security.kind.passkey_available.text: According to the Passkeys Directory these sites support passkeys. Passkeys cannot be phished or reused.
security.kind.passkey_available.fix: Create a passkey in the website's security settings; Passbox saves it in this login.
security.kind.duplicate.title: Duplicate items
security.kind.duplicate.summary: The same account saved more than once.
security.kind.duplicate.text: Several items have the same website and username (or card number). After a password change, one of them is outdated.
security.kind.duplicate.fix: Compare the items and move the outdated ones to the trash.
security.kind.missing_url.title: Without website
security.kind.missing_url.summary: Logins Passbox can't match to a site.
security.kind.missing_url.text: Without a website address, autofill and phishing protection can't work for these logins.
security.kind.missing_url.fix: Add the address of the sign-in page.
security.kind.missing_username.title: Without username
security.kind.missing_username.text: These logins have a password but no username or email address.
security.kind.missing_username.fix: Add the username so autofill can fill both fields.
security.kind.totp_in_same_item.title: Both factors in one place
security.kind.totp_in_same_item.summary: Password and one-time code in the same item.
security.kind.totp_in_same_item.text: Convenient and still far safer than no 2FA, but whoever opens your vault has both factors. That is a trade-off, not a mistake.
security.kind.totp_in_same_item.fix: For your most important accounts, consider a security key or a separate authenticator app.
alias.title: Email alias
alias.text: Sign up with a new address that forwards to your inbox, so websites never learn your real email and you can turn off one that gets spam.
alias.privacy: Passbox asks {provider} directly from this device; your Passbox server isn't involved.
alias.whereKey: Where to find the key at {provider}
alias.serverHint: Only if you host the service yourself.
alias.storeHint: The key is saved as an item in your vault, encrypted like your passwords and synced to your devices.
alias.error.unauthorized: {provider} rejected the API key. Check the key in the service item.
alias.error.rate_limited: {provider} asks you to wait before creating more aliases.
alias.error.failed: {provider} couldn't create an alias. Try again later.
alias.error.no_alias: {provider} answered without an alias. Check your plan with the service.
alias.error.insecure_url: The server address must start with https://.
alias.error.no_key: The service item has no API key.
alias.error.network: {provider} couldn't be reached. Some services block requests from web pages; then use the browser extension or the desktop app.
settings.websiteIconsDescription: Loads the icons of the websites in your vault through your Passbox server, so the websites never see this device. Your server learns which websites you saved; the contents stay encrypted.
settings.websiteIconsOff: Your Passbox server doesn't load website icons, so Passbox shows initials instead.
